output.question: Find the top trending Go, TypeScript, and Zig repositories this week relevant to agentic, MCP, or dev-tooling.
output.findings:
In the Go ecosystem, momentum is driven by AI agent infrastructure. 'BenedictKing/ccx' (1,004 stars this week) provides a high-performance API proxy for LLMs. 'Armur-Ai/Pentest-Swarm-AI' (324 stars) and 'Gentleman-Programming/engram' (305 stars) highlight the trend toward autonomous agent swarms and persistent memory systems for AI coding agents. Google's 'google/ax' (423 stars) is also gaining traction as a distributed agent runtime.

TypeScript repositories are dominated by tools enhancing AI coding workflows. 'Lum1104/Understand-Anything' (19,223 stars) and 'colbymchenry/codegraph' (12,380 stars) are rapidly trending for their ability to provide code knowledge graphs for LLMs. 'can1357/oh-my-pi' (2,122 stars) and 'EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin' (1,831 stars) focus on agentic terminal integration and plugin specifications for AI coding assistants.

Zig repositories show strong interest in high-performance tooling for AI and infrastructure. 'ghostty-org/ghostty' (514 stars) remains a top-tier terminal emulator, while 'lightpanda-io/browser' (199 stars) is gaining attention as a headless browser specifically optimized for AI automation. 'tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle' (119 stars) continues to be a critical infrastructure project for high-performance financial data, and 'zml/zml' (26 stars) is emerging as a Zig-based framework for hardware-agnostic machine learning.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the specific sub-question/task from the INPUTS list (look at the first literal value). If no specific task is in the INPUTS, read the overall USER_QUERY. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`, default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, total stars, stars gained (or weekly/monthly stars depending on the window), and URL. In your `findings`, list each repo clearly with its description, total stars, and stars gained so that downstream nodes can extract these fields.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
